newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close up, Hanbo hearing has no impact.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close up, Hanbo hearing has no impact.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed slightly higher on Friday on the back of gains by individual theme-backed stocks, brokers said.
The composite index ended up 1.68 points at 692.48, after fluctuating between 687.41 and 693.97.
The testimony by President Kim Young-sam's son, Hyun-chul, at a parliamentary hearing was a major concern but had little direct impact on trading.
Jinro Ltd closed off from early lows on hopes of a quick profit on the stock. Blue chips fell on profit-taking in response to gains early this week.
"Trading was focused mainly on small-cap stocks backed by speculation or rumours," said Park Byung-moon, head of research at LG Securities.
Kim Hyun-chul testified before the parliamentary hearing on allegations that he had played a role in the loans-for-kickbacks scandal surrounding the failed Hanbo Steel Co.
He denied taking bribes in connection with the scandal which has rocked the local financial markets since early this year.
Troubled Jinro Ltd closed at 7,550 won, down 140 won from Thursday's close, after hitting its 1997 low of 7,080 won.

Jinro topped the most actives list, with 2.12 million shares changing hands, against just 9,970 shares traded on Thursday. Brokers said buyers believed they could make money at the current price, down 60 percent from 1997 high of 19,000.
Segye Corp rose 730 won to its limit of 9,910 on talk, denied by a company official, that the company had finalised a plan to develop a huge tract of its land.
Keumkang Development was unmoved by ING-Baring's announcement that it had revised downward its forecasts for Keumkang's recurring profit in 1997 and 1998. It closed up 100 won at 12,100.
Brokers said institutional investors were inactive on worries about increasing margin loans, now at this year's highest level of three trillion won.
"Institutions are concerned that a big rise in the index could spark heavy selling as many people regard 700 as their selling point," said a Hyundai Securities broker.
Samsung Electronics fell 1,100 won to 58,500 and Pohang Iron and Steel shed 200 won to 53,500.
